sub_topic.name: DNA & Inheritance
sub_topic.sub_subject_name: Life Sciences (Living Systems Designed with Purpose & Order)
sub_topic.description: 13-year academic progression (K-12) for DNA & Inheritance in Genetics, Reproduction & Adaptation (Science & Nature)

objectives.sub_subject_name: Life Sciences (Living Systems Designed with Purpose & Order)
objectives.objective_text: Observe that young plants and animals resemble their parents but are not exactly the same.

standards: NGSS 3-LS3-1 — Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parent (grades 3)

objectives.sub_subject_name: Life Sciences (Living Systems Designed with Purpose & Order)
objectives.objective_text: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.

standards: NGSS 3-LS3-1 — Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parent (grades 3)

objectives.sub_subject_name: Life Sciences (Living Systems Designed with Purpose & Order)
objectives.objective_text: Describe how genes located on chromosomes carry the instructions passed from parents to offspring.

standards: NGSS MS-LS3-1 — Genes are located in the chromosomes of cells, with each chromosome pair containing two variants of each (grades 6-8)

objectives.sub_subject_name: Life Sciences (Living Systems Designed with Purpose & Order)
objectives.objective_text: Explain how genes control the production of specific proteins, and how mutations can change proteins and thereby change traits.

standards: NGSS MS-LS3-1 — Genes are located in the chromosomes of cells, with each chromosome pair containing two variants of each (grades 6-8)

objectives.sub_subject_name: Life Sciences (Living Systems Designed with Purpose & Order)
objectives.objective_text: Ask questions to clarify the role of DNA and chromosomes in coding the instructions for traits passed from parents to offspring.

standards: NGSS HS-LS3-1 — Ask questions to clarify relationships about the role of DNA and chromosomes in coding the instructions  (grades 9-12)
